mechanism_steps.summary: The Co(II)-C bond of the B12 cofactor undergoes homoloysis, forming the adenosyl radical and Co(I).
The adenosyl radical abstracts a hydrogen from the substrate.
The substrate radical attacks its own carbonyl carbon, forcing the radical onto the oxygen, which deprotonates His244.
His244 deprotonates the oxygen, which causes radical rearrangement and the cleavage of the propane ring formed, the radical ends up on the newly formed CH<sub>2</sub> branch.
The substrate radical abstracts a hydrogen from the adenosine, re-forming the adenosyl radical.
The adenosyl radical and Co(I) undergo colligation, reforming the B12 cofactor.

records.label: TEM-1 class A serine beta-lactamase source mechanism

mechanism_steps.summary: Glu166 deprotonates a conserved water molecule which in turn deprotonates the nucleophilic Ser70, initiating the nucleophilic addition onto the carbonyl carbon of the beta-lactam, forming a tetrahedral intermediate.
The tetrahedral intermediate collapses, cleaving the C-N bond in the beta-lactam, the nitrogen deprotonates Ser130.
Ser130 deprotonates water, which in turn deprotonates Glu166.
Glu166 deprotonates water, which initiates a nucleophilic addition at the carbonyl carbon, forming a new tetrahedral intermediate.
The tetrahedral intermediate collapses, cleaving the acyl-enzyme bond and liberating Ser70, which in turn deprotonates the Glu166.

records.label: TEM-1 class A serine beta-lactamase grounded hypothesis

mechanism_steps.summary: In the preferred source proposal, Glu166 activates a conserved water relay that deprotonates Ser70 (P62593 natural Ser68) as it attacks the beta-lactam carbonyl to form a tetrahedral intermediate.
Collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate opens the beta-lactam C-N bond and leaves the substrate covalently acylated to Ser70, with the source assigning coupled proton transfer through Ser130.
The source proposal resets the Ser130/Glu166 proton network through water before deacylation.
Glu166 activates water for nucleophilic attack on the acyl-enzyme carbonyl, forming a second tetrahedral intermediate.
Collapse of the second tetrahedral intermediate cleaves the acyl-enzyme bond, releases hydrolyzed product, and regenerates Ser70/Glu166 states.
